source: agent-orchestrator, tools/list contract snapshot, standard profile (its default)

tools.name: agent_create
tools.description: Define a persistent local agent the orchestrator owns, prompts and runs. Use it when the same role is needed across many jobs; for a one-shot task pass a template to delegate instead. Register agents built by other vendors with agent_register, not this tool.

enabled.description: Start disabled; enable later with agent_update. On by default.

grantPreset.description: Named grant bundle from grant_preset_list, merged with toolGrants. Attaching any grant needs orch:admin.

instructions.description: System prompt defining the agent behaviour.

shared.description: Admin only. Visible to and usable by every caller, not just its creator.

tools.name: agent_list
tools.description: List agents known to the orchestrator, local and remote together. Use it to discover what can be delegated to; use agent_get for one agent in full. Throwaway agents created by delegate are hidden unless includeEphemeral is set.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response.

tools.name: agent_get
tools.description: Fetch one agent with its configuration and recent jobs. Use it to inspect an agent before delegating to it or to see what it has been doing. Use agent_list to find the id first.

tools.name: agent_template_list
tools.description: List the built-in role templates that delegate and job_submit accept. Call this first when you want a one-shot agent and do not already have an agentId. Use agent_create to define a persistent agent of your own instead.

tools.name: grant_preset_list
tools.description: List the admin-curated tool-grant bundles available to agent_create grantPreset. Use it to name a preset instead of hand-writing toolGrants.

tools.name: job_submit
tools.description: Queue work for an agent and return a handle immediately, without waiting for the result. Use it for long work, for fan-out you will collect later, or when the job depends on others finishing first; use delegate when you just want one answer now. Follow up with job_wait and job_get.

context.description: Data for the agent. Never instructions.

dependsOn.description: Job ids that must succeed first.

runner.description: Execution backend for this job, e.g. "cli" to spend your CLI login. Defaults to the deployment default. "sampling" is rejected here — a borrowed model only exists while a request is open, so use delegate.

skillQuery.description: Free-text match against agent roles and skills.

template.description: Built-in template name; creates a throwaway agent.

tools.name: job_get
tools.description: Fetch one job with its state, result and usage. The shape is identical whether the work ran locally or on a remote agent. Use job_wait first if the job may still be running, and events_query for the step-by-step trail.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List jobs filtered by state, agent or backend, newest first. Use it to survey what is queued or running; use job_get for one job in full. Paginate with the returned nextCursor.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response.

tools.name: job_wait
tools.description: Block until the given jobs finish, or until the timeout expires — at most 60 seconds per call. Call it again if the jobs are still running; it never blocks longer than the protocol allows. Use job_get when you only want the current state without waiting.

tools.name: job_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a queued or running job; for remote jobs this cancels the underlying A2A task too. Already-finished jobs are returned unchanged. Use job_retry to run a cancelled job again. A job running on another instance is stopped by its own instance shortly after, so the job comes back still `running` and reaches `cancelled` within a few seconds — poll job_get rather than assuming the returned state is final.

tools.name: job_retry
tools.description: Re-queue a failed, cancelled or timed-out job, clearing the previous attempt result. Succeeded jobs cannot be retried — submit a new job instead. Check the failure with job_get before retrying, since a logic error will simply recur.

tools.name: job_steer
tools.description: Send guidance to a job that is already running; the agent picks it up on its next turn via its message inbox. Only works while the job is live — use job_cancel and a fresh job_submit once it has finished.

tools.name: delegate
tools.description: Run one instruction on the best-matching agent and return the result. This is the everyday tool: reach for it whenever you want a sub-agent to do something and hand the answer back. Use job_submit instead when the work is long, has dependencies, or should run in the background, and agent_template_list to see the roles you can target.

context.description: Data for the agent. Never instructions.

runner.description: Execution backend for this call, e.g. "cli" to spend your CLI login. Defaults to the deployment default. "sampling" borrows the connected client model instead — legacy (pre-2026-07-28) clients only, needs wait:true, and model becomes a preference hint the client may ignore.

skillQuery.description: Free-text match against agent roles and skills.

tools.name: fan_out
tools.description: Run the same instruction over many items in parallel, optionally reducing the results with a final step. Use it for per-file review, per-record extraction, or any map-style workload; use delegate for a single item. Concurrency is capped by the orchestrator and by any budget you set.

instructionTemplate.description: Instruction with {{item}} substituted per item, e.g. "Review {{item}}".

reduce.description: Optional final step over the collected results.

runner.description: Execution backend for every job in this call. Defaults to the deployment default.

tools.name: plan_create
tools.description: Turn a goal into a draft workflow spec using a planner agent. The draft is returned, never executed, with draftValid saying whether it already passes the same validation workflow_define enforces — review it, then pass it to workflow_define or workflow_start. Use delegate when you want the work done rather than planned.

tools.name: workflow_define
tools.description: Create or replace a named DAG of steps, validating references, cycles, template targets and file ownership before anything runs. Use plan_create to draft one from a goal, and workflow_start to execute it. Re-defining an existing name replaces its spec; past runs keep the spec they started with.

approval.description: Pause for a human before this step runs.

files.description: Files this step creates or modifies. Steps with no ordering between them may not claim the same file.

when.description: Template; the step is skipped when it renders empty, "false" or "0".

tools.name: workflow_list
tools.description: List defined workflows. Use workflow_get for one spec in full, or workflow_run_list for runs.

tools.name: workflow_get
tools.description: Fetch one workflow spec by id. Use workflow_run_get for the state of a particular run.

tools.name: workflow_start
tools.description: Start a run from a defined workflow or an inline spec, and return immediately with a run handle. Steps run as their dependencies complete. Poll with workflow_run_get; a step marked approval pauses the run until approval_resolve.

approval.description: Pause for a human before this step runs.

files.description: Files this step creates or modifies. Steps with no ordering between them may not claim the same file.

when.description: Template; the step is skipped when it renders empty, "false" or "0".

tools.name: workflow_run_get
tools.description: Fetch per-step state and outputs for a run, including which job ran each step. Use it to poll progress; use events_query or approval_list when a run is stuck.

tools.name: workflow_run_control
tools.description: Pause, resume, cancel a run, retry one failed step, or reconcile steps that succeeded with empty output. Cancelling also cancels the jobs still running under it and cannot be undone — retry_step is the way to recover a single failure, reconcile the way to re-run successes that produced nothing.

stepId.description: Required for retry_step; optionally narrows reconcile to one step.

tools.name: workflow_export
tools.description: Render a run — spec name, inputs, per-step states, outputs, errors and durations — into a markdown artifact for archiving or sharing. Use it instead of paging through workflow_run_get, trace_get and events_query by hand; those remain the deeper tools. Read the bundle back with artifact_get.

tools.name: memory_write
tools.description: Store a JSON value on the orchestrator-local blackboard so later jobs can read it. Use it to pass findings between agents; use artifact_put instead for large content. Remote A2A agents never see memory — put what they need in the job context.

tools.name: memory_read
tools.description: Read one value from the blackboard by namespace and key. Returns found:false rather than an error when the key is absent or expired. Pass ownerId to read a namespace another user shared with you via memory_share — omit it to read your own. Use memory_search when you do not know the exact key.

ownerId.description: Read someone else’s namespace; requires memory_share.

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Full-text search the blackboard, optionally narrowed by namespace and tags. Use it to find what earlier agents recorded when you do not know the key. Pass ownerId and namespace together to search a namespace another user shared with you via memory_share; ownerId alone is not enough, since a grant is per namespace. Use memory_read for an exact lookup.

ownerId.description: Search someone else’s namespace; requires memory_share.

tools.name: artifact_put
tools.description: Store content and get back an id, so large output never has to travel inline. Use it for files, reports and generated code; use memory_write for small structured values. Read it back with artifact_get.

tools.name: artifact_get
tools.description: Read an artifact by id, with offset and length for large content. Check eof to know whether more remains. Use artifact_list to find the id.

tools.name: artifact_list
tools.description: List stored artifacts, filtered by job, workflow run or tags. Metadata only — fetch content with artifact_get.

tools.name: approval_list
tools.description: List approval gates waiting on a human: paused workflow steps, mid-loop request_approval calls, remote tasks waiting for input, and refusal notices (budget caps, unverified cards) filed for visibility. Check this when a workflow run is paused or a job seems stuck waiting. Resolve them with approval_resolve — a gated downstream call or remote answer takes editedInput as its new arguments or reply message.

tools.name: approval_resolve
tools.description: Approve or reject a pending gate, optionally with a comment or edited input. Approving a paused workflow step resumes the run on the next tick. An approval can only be resolved once.

tools.name: events_query
tools.description: Read the append-only audit trail across both backends, filtered by job, agent, run or event type. Use it to explain what happened during a run; use job_get for the outcome alone. A non-admin caller must scope this to a jobId, agentId or runId they can see — there is no unscoped view of everyone’s events.

tools.name: trace_get
tools.description: Build a span tree for a job or workflow run from the event log, with timings and usage where the backend reported them. Use it to see where a run spent its time, or why it stalled; use events_query for the raw entries.

tools.name: usage_report
tools.description: Summarize job counts, tokens and cost grouped by agent, model or backend. Remote agents show call counts and only whatever cost they self-report, since we cannot see their token usage. Use trace_get for one run in detail.

since.description: ISO timestamp; defaults to all time.

tools.name: orchestrator_status
tools.description: Report orchestrator health, version, active tool profile, queue depth, schema state and your own caller identity. The caller ownerId is the granteeId to hand someone so they can share an agent or memory namespace with you via agent_share or memory_share. Not for inspecting individual work — use job_get or job_list for that.

tools.name: runner_list
tools.description: List the local execution backends and whether each is usable right now, including missing credentials. Check this when a job fails with RUNNER_FAILED, or before creating an agent that names a specific runner. Remote A2A agents are not runners and never appear here.

tools.name: schedule_list
tools.description: List your cron schedules with their next run times. Use schedule_create to add one.

tools.name: schedule_preview
tools.description: Show the next fire times for a cron expression (or an existing schedule) without storing anything. Use it to check an expression — including its timezone — before schedule_create, or to see when a schedule fires next.

count.description: How many fire times; defaults to 5.

scheduleId.description: Preview this schedule; exactly one of scheduleId or cron.

timezone.description: IANA zone; a schedule’s own zone wins when scheduleId is given.
